verdict_reason: Solid coverage of the reject path and problem+json body, but the no-PII-in-logs assertion is vacuous and the filter's MDC-cleanup finally block is untested.

todos.issue: The no-PII-in-logs assertion is vacuous: IdentityHeaderFilter only logs inside reject(), so on this happy path appender.list is empty and allSatisfy() passes over zero events — the test would stay green if the filter logged the request body verbatim.
todos.fix: Exercise the path that actually logs (omit the org header so log.warn in reject() fires) and add assertThat(appender.list).isNotEmpty() before the allSatisfy, so the PII guard has real events to inspect.

todos.issue: No test pins the filter's finally { MDC.remove(organisationId) } — RecordingChain only snapshots the MDC during the chain, and nothing asserts the key is gone after doFilter returns or when the chain throws, so an MDC leak onto a pooled servlet thread (org A's id tagging org B's log lines) would go undetected.
todos.fix: After the doFilter call assert MDC.get("organisationId") is null, and add a test where the chain throws (FilterChain that throws ServletException) asserting the key is still removed.

todos.issue: In nonOrganisationPathsBypassTheFilterEntirely the status-200 assertion is self-fulfilling — RecordingChain.doFilter sets 200 itself and MockHttpServletResponse already defaults to 200, so the assertion cannot fail regardless of what the filter does.
todos.fix: Drop the status assertion (chain.wasCalled() is the real bypass proof) or assert the negative that actually matters: response.getStatus() is not 400 and the body is empty.

todos.issue: None of the seven test methods use the mandated explicit // Given, // When, // Then comment blocks that every other unit test in the codebase follows.
todos.fix: Add // Given, // When, // Then (or // When & Then for the short ones) to each test method.
